logo.title: The Posy.
logo.lead: A four-petal bloom in a round frame, like a posy seen from above or a wreath. It suits both a wedding invitation and a sympathy card, which matters for a florist that does both. The wordmark is set in Prata, an elegant, slightly old-fashioned serif.

story.title: Roman Road's florist since 1950.
story.lead: Mr Dennington opened his flower shop on Roman Road in 1950. In the 1970s it passed to a new family, and the grandson of the man who took it over still works there today. It's known across the East End for wedding and funeral flowers. The brand should feel graceful and dependable, a florist you trust with the biggest days of your life.
story.positioning: The East End's wedding and funeral florist. Family-run on Roman Road since 1950.

colour.title: Violet, cream, marigold.
colour.lead: Deep violet has a quiet dignity that suits both celebrations and remembrance. Cream is soft and marigold is warmth, used only on dark backgrounds or as a detail. Lilac mist is for panels.

type.title: Graceful serif, friendly sans.
type.lead: Prata is elegant and warm for headlines and card messages. Mulish is soft and easy to read for prices and ordering details. Both are free on Google Fonts.

samples.label: Body
samples.text: Tell us about your day and we'll design flowers around it.

voice.title: Warm, calm, reassuring.
voice.lead: Talk like a florist who has done a thousand weddings and a thousand funerals: calm, kind and practical. Celebrate joyfully and comfort quietly.
pairs: "Tell us about your day and we'll design around it."
"We'll help you choose something that feels right."

imagery.title: Blooms, hands, Roman Road.
imagery.lead: Wedding bouquets and buttonholes in soft natural light, respectful close-ups of tribute work, the Roman Road shopfront on market day, and the family at the bench. No glossy stock bouquets.
